Liz Truss is the shortest-serving Prime Minister in the history of the United Kingdom [d1][d3][d4]. She became Prime Minister on 6 September 2022 and resigned just 44–45 days later, after a disastrous "mini-budget" spooked financial markets and caused her political support to collapse [d3][d5][d6]. Before Truss, the record was held by George Canning, who served 119 days in 1827 before dying in office [d2][d4][d5]. The previous record before Canning was even more obscure: William Pulteney served only two days and James Waldegrave only five days in the 18th century, but neither actually formed a government, so they are not generally counted as true prime ministries [d2].
